note: The vendor states that every attribute and relationship carries Source (where the data comes from) and Owner (who owns it) metadata plus a protected flag, and that every object records created_at, created_by, updated_at and updated_by. The vendor states that each value and relationship is stored with the period during which it applied, and that a query with a branch and a timestamp (the GraphQL `at` parameter) returns the data that was valid at that time. These validity periods are recorded from changes; no page states that a user can set a validity period of their own, such as a future start or end date for a value.

The vendor states that related changes can be grouped on one branch so that a single merge applies them to the default branch, and that a merge either completes or is rolled back; the merge page also states that a merge is not one database transaction. The vendor states that checks are user-defined validation logic that run on a proposed change, and that a proposed change cannot be merged if a check does not complete successfully. The vendor states that each change creates a new timestamped version and that data can be read on any branch as it existed at an earlier time; no page states that a single GraphQL mutation outside a branch merge runs as one transaction.
